title: Passage an adherent line to a target density
summary: Inspect and harvest a synthetic adherent culture, verify a two-chamber viable count, plan two T-75 flasks by target viable-cell number, and complete passage and PDL records.
scenario: A generic synthetic non-human adherent mammalian culture is ready for a target-density passage exercise. Routine runs begin at 72–84% confluence; some seeded runs reveal 95% confluence and must be refused rather than passaged under the scenario rule. Use a calcium/magnesium-free wash, enzyme-based dissociation, observed detachment and complete-medium neutralization. Count two synthetic chambers, then seed two T-75 flasks with 500,000 viable cells each in 12.0 mL final volume per flask.
guided_steps: Inspect the monolayer and enter its displayed confluence. The routine teaching window is 70–85%; a displayed 95% culture must use the over-confluent disposition rather than routine passaging.
For a routine culture, remove the spent medium and wash with 15 mL calcium/magnesium-free balanced salt solution.
Add 3.75 mL enzyme-based dissociation reagent and incubate for 2 min. The model's teaching bound is 1–5 min, not a cell-line acceptance limit.
Inspect detachment and enter the displayed percentage. At least 90% must be detached before neutralization.
Neutralize with 7.5 mL complete medium, then collect at 200 × g for 5 min and resuspend in 6.0 mL.
Prepare 10 µL suspension plus 10 µL trypan blue. Record the displayed included tallies for chambers A and B.
Viable cells/mL = mean included unstained cells per chamber × 10,000 × dilution factor; viability = unstained/all included cells × 100.
Plan two flasks with 500,000 viable cells per flask and 12.0 mL final volume per flask. V_cells = N_target/C_viable; V_fresh = V_final − V_cells.
Seed according to the recorded plan, increment passage 12 to 13, and compute PDL increment log₂(Nf/N0) from viable yield and N0 = 1,815,000. Add that increment to previous cumulative PDL 18.
Record 37 °C, 5% CO₂ and 24 h for the synthetic incubation and submit for a formative debrief. No growth outcome is predicted.

checkpoints.description: Keep dissociation exposure within the 1–5 min teaching bound.
checkpoints.rationale: Excess exposure lowers viability in the synthetic model; longer is not automatically better.

checkpoints.description: Observe at least 90% detachment before neutralization.
checkpoints.rationale: Neutralizing too early leaves an unrepresentative attached fraction; extended exposure is not a substitute for observation.

checkpoints.description: Add 7.5 mL complete medium before collection and counting.
checkpoints.rationale: The complete-medium step limits continued dissociation activity before viable counting and seeding.

checkpoints.rationale: A defined collection and final volume make the viable-yield calculation auditable.

sources.use: General adherent harvest workflow, wash and reagent scaling, detachment observation, neutralization, collection and cell-line-specific cautions; link-only reference, no text copied.
Conceptual contrast in the lesson only: suspension cells are sampled and diluted without substrate detachment. The simulator does not model suspension passaging.
Target cell-number/final-volume seeding relationship, routine growth-phase and recordkeeping context, and repeated-subculture limitations; link-only reference.

limitations: All cells, microscopy panels, tallies and results are synthetic and non-human. The model rehearses decisions and arithmetic only.
The simulator does not establish competency, aseptic hand skill, microscopy skill, institutional authorisation or physical validation of a passage protocol.
Confluence thresholds, exact T-75 volumes, exposure bound, viability penalties, target density, PDL convention and numerical tolerances are teaching choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria.
The viability penalties are deterministic tally transformations, not validated dissociation kinetics, membrane biology or growth predictions.
Dye exclusion represents membrane integrity at the count only; it does not establish future growth, identity, phenotype, genomic stability or sterility.
Suspension passaging is explained in the linked lesson but is outside this simulator. Shaking, spinner vessels, direct-versus-pellet dilution choices and suspension growth are not modelled.
The 24 h incubation is a record field only. No attachment, proliferation, phenotype, contamination or future-viability outcome is inferred.
